description: Passing NULL as a CALL argument, or through a SET value, must bind a REAL SQL null and not the string 'NULL' - so :param IS NULL is true and :param IS NOT NULL is false. The consequence that matters is the common guard IF (:x IS NOT NULL AND NOT is_allowed(:x)): it must NOT fire when a NULL is passed, which is asserted here through a three-parameter procedure whose optional last argument is NULL. A NULL arriving from a SESSION VARIABLE binds the same way, and a column DEFAULT NULL still reads back as NULL. Converted 1:1 from scripting/NullArgumentBindingTest (now retired).

steps.sql: CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE nat(p VARCHAR) RETURNS VARCHAR LANGUAGE SQL AS $$ BEGIN RETURN IFF(:p IS NULL, 'NULL', 'NOT_NULL'); END $$
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION is_allowed(x VARCHAR) RETURNS BOOLEAN LANGUAGE SQL AS $$ UPPER(x) IN ('A','B','C','D','E') $$

CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE save(p_a VARCHAR, p_b VARCHAR, p_c VARCHAR) RETURNS VARCHAR LANGUAGE SQL AS $$ DECLARE bad EXCEPTION (-20001, 'not allowed'); BEGIN IF (NOT is_allowed(:p_b)) THEN RAISE bad; END IF; IF (:p_a IS NOT NULL AND NOT is_allowed(:p_a)) THEN RAISE bad; END IF; IF (:p_c IS NOT NULL AND NOT is_allowed(:p_c)) THEN RAISE bad; END IF; RETURN 'ok'; END $$
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE echo(p VARCHAR) RETURNS VARCHAR LANGUAGE SQL AS $$ BEGIN RETURN IFF(:p IS NULL, 'NULL', 'NOT_NULL'); END $$
SET v = (SELECT CASE WHEN 1 = 2 THEN 'x' END)
